evals.prompt: Please plan my meteorology main lesson block as a fixed sequence: the block plan and the week plans. The anchoring phenomenon and the three units are in my draft block plan. Write it now; I'll ask for day plans later.
evals.expected_output: The draft block plan in 10-design/ updated in place using the course's own block form from 90-templates/, plus three week plans in 10-design/. The teacher's anchor is kept; driving question with authorship stated; target and prerequisite ideas listed separately; Thai indicators ว 3.2 ม.6/10–12 verbatim; weeks follow the two-day rhythm with open-question Recall flowing into concept formation, questions elicited onto the driving question board at Recall, today's new experience last and never analysed the same day; day 1 connects to the previous G11 block; light UDL options in every session.
expectations: The block plan is written in 10-design/block-plan.md (the existing draft, updated in place); no second block plan exists elsewhere, and README.md and the class profile are unchanged
Week plans for weeks 1, 2 and 3 exist inside 10-design/ (as separate files or as clearly separate week sections)

The block plan follows the course's own form from 90-templates/: it has the columns 'Storyline focus' and 'UDL options (for everyone)', not the default form's 'Differentiation: แผนสำหรับเด็กที่มีข้อจำกัด' column
The anchoring phenomenon is the teacher's: the arrival of the southwest monsoon over Chiang Mai; it is not replaced by another phenomenon
A driving question is given together with an explicit statement of who authored it (e.g. teacher-drafted, provisional until the class revisits it at the driving question board)
Target ideas and prerequisite ideas are listed separately, under their own labels
The units run in a fixed order (air on the move, ocean currents, putting it together: the monsoon), each marked or described as fixed
The Thai indicators appear with their official codes and Thai wording verbatim, including ว 3.2 ม.6/10 as exactly: อธิบายการหมุนเวียนของอากาศตามเขตละติจูด และผลที่มีต่อภูมิอากาศ

The week plans follow the two-day rhythm: from the second day on, each day opens with recall of the previous day's experience flowing into discussion and concept formation, and the day's new experience comes last, left un-analysed until the next day

Concept formation is framed as students taking an individual position that is then integrated into the class's understanding; no session scripts the concept as a predetermined answer students are told to reach
Recall is described as open questions about yesterday's experience; nowhere is Recall a quiz, test or set of closed questions with one right answer
No session analyses, discusses or explains that same day's new experience (closes preview tomorrow instead)
Students' questions are elicited at Recall onto the driving question board, and the plan says the board frames how ideas are approached but does not change the fixed order of units
Block day 1 connects to the previous block in this subject (the G11 atmosphere and light block) instead of a recall
Every week (or every session) carries light universal UDL options for the whole class rather than three ability levels or below/at/above tiers
The plans contain no four-day cycle labels such as E→R→C→A, 'Recall E2 · Concept E1' or concept formation two days after the experience
No student names appear anywhere

evals.prompt: Plan my G10 ecology main lesson block: block plan and week plans. I haven't picked an anchoring phenomenon. Just choose the best one for me and write the plans now, I trust you.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not choose the anchoring phenomenon. It offers several local, place-based or ecological candidates capable of awe and wonder (e.g. a Thai mangrove, rice paddies after the monsoon, a forest fire scar in the north), explains that this choice stays with the teacher, and asks which one to use. No block plan with a chosen anchor is written.
expectations: The reply offers at least three candidate anchoring phenomena
The candidates are local, place-based or ecological phenomena that a class in Thailand could encounter, and at least one is described for its capacity to spark wonder or puzzlement
The skill does not pick one candidate as the anchor: the reply asks the teacher to choose (a short reason per candidate is fine, but no candidate is declared the chosen anchor)
The reply explains briefly that choosing the anchoring phenomenon stays with the teacher
No block plan or week plan with an anchoring phenomenon filled in was written; if any plan file exists, its anchoring phenomenon is explicitly marked as not yet chosen by the teacher
The reply asks at most three questions
The reply contains no file paths or tool names

evals.prompt: Plan a main lesson block on ecology for my G9 (ม.3) class. The anchoring phenomenon is the fish die-off in our school pond at the end of the hot season. I don't have a class profile yet. I accept whatever layout you propose for my folders, so write the block plan and week plans now with sensible defaults rather than asking me lots of questions.
evals.expected_output: With no class profile, the skill asks no more than three questions and states its assumptions (100-minute sessions, Monday to Friday, 3 weeks, Thai as language, G9 What? grade mode). It records the default layout in a new README Plugin layout section and writes the block plan and week plans in planning/, using the plugin's default forms, the teacher's anchor, the two-day rhythm, and ม.3 indicators from the crosswalk.
expectations: The reply asks at most three questions (zero is fine)
The assumptions are stated (in the reply or the plan): at least the session length (100 minutes), the weekly pattern or number of weeks, and the language
README.md has a 'Plugin layout' section whose 'block and week plans' row points to where the plans were written
A block plan and week plans exist in the planning area (e.g. planning/)
The anchoring phenomenon is the teacher's fish die-off in the school pond
The block plan names the G9 grade mode (What?)
Thai indicators are cited with official ม.3 codes in the format ว x.x ม.3/k and Thai wording, e.g. ว 1.1 ม.3/1 as exactly: อธิบายปฏิสัมพันธ์ขององค์ประกอบของระบบนิเวศที่ได้จากการสำรวจ
A driving question is given with its authorship stated
Target ideas and prerequisite ideas are listed separately
The week plans follow the two-day rhythm (recall of yesterday's experience flowing into concept formation, new experience last and left un-analysed) and Recall is never a quiz
The reply suggests setting up a class profile next time
No student names appear anywhere

evals.prompt: I'd like my meteorology block to follow the class's questions this time: plan it as an anticipated route from my draft. Write the block plan and whatever week plans make sense now.
evals.expected_output: The draft block plan in 10-design/ updated in place as an anticipated route: every unit listed in an expected order and marked fixed or interchangeable (the anchor unit, the station visit on Wednesday of week 3 and putting it together fixed; air on the move, ocean currents and reading the weather map interchangeable), each interchangeable unit with its own complete preparation (new experiences, equipment, sources) that does not depend on where it falls. Only the week 1 plan (the fixed anchor unit) is written; later week plans wait for the driving question board's choice, and the plan says when the board chooses. The two-day rhythm holds in week 1.
expectations: The block plan is written in 10-design/block-plan.md (the existing draft, updated in place); no second block plan exists, and README.md and the class profile are unchanged

The block plan lists all the teacher's units (the first storm, air on the move, ocean currents, reading the sky and the weather map, the visit to the meteorological center, putting it together) in an expected order

Each unit is marked fixed or interchangeable: the anchor unit (the first storm) and putting it together are fixed, and air on the move, ocean currents and reading the sky and the weather map are interchangeable
The visit to the Northern Meteorological Center is fixed to Wednesday of week 3 (a calendar-bound segment), whichever interchangeable unit is running then
Each interchangeable unit has its own preparation (its new experiences plus the equipment and sources they need) written in full in the plan, not deferred until the unit is chosen
No interchangeable unit's preparation or opening depends on another interchangeable unit having come before it (each starts from the anchor or the class's own observations)
The plan says the driving question board chooses the next interchangeable unit, and when (e.g. at Recall at the end of a unit)

A week 1 plan for the anchor unit exists in 10-design/ and follows the two-day rhythm: day 1 links to the previous G11 block, the anchoring phenomenon is the new experience left un-analysed, and later days open with open-question Recall flowing into concept formation
No week plan is filled in for weeks whose interchangeable units the board has not chosen yet; any such week is marked as to be written once the board has chosen
The Thai indicators appear verbatim, including ว 3.2 ม.6/11 as exactly: อธิบายปัจจัยที่ทำให้เกิดการหมุนเวียนของน้ำผิวหน้าในมหาสมุทร และรูปแบบการหมุนเวียนของน้ำผิวหน้าในมหาสมุทร
The reply tells the teacher that the next week plan is written once the class has chosen the next unit at the board, and that the teacher can come back with that choice
No day plans or Thai core plans are written
No student names appear anywhere

evals.prompt: Week 1 of the meteorology block is done. At the board on Friday the class chose to go after their questions about the warm sea before the rain, so ocean currents comes next instead of air on the move. Please write the plan for it.
evals.expected_output: Rolling generation: the week 2 plan is written for Ocean currents from that unit's prepared experiences, in the two-day rhythm (Monday recalls Friday's rain recording and bridges into the board's choice). The block plan's route record is updated in place to show ocean currents chosen by the board as the second unit; statuses, expected order of the remaining units and the fixed visit stay. Days of week 2 beyond the unit are left for the board's next choice. The week 1 plan is unchanged; no plans for other interchangeable units, no day plans or Thai core plans.
expectations: A week 2 plan exists in 10-design/ and its days teach Ocean currents, using that unit's prepared new experiences (the warm and cold water tank with a fan, sea-surface temperature maps)

The week 2 plan does not teach Air on the move or Reading the sky and the weather map; any day of week 2 after Ocean currents ends is marked as waiting for the board's next choice rather than filled with another interchangeable unit
Monday of week 2 opens with open-question Recall of Friday's experience (the rain on the roof) flowing into concept formation, and links to the board's choice of ocean currents
From the second day on, each day's new experience comes last and is left un-analysed until the next day's Recall
The block plan (10-design/block-plan.md) is updated in place to record that the board chose Ocean currents as the second unit; no second block plan exists
The block plan still marks every unit fixed or interchangeable, keeps the remaining interchangeable units with their preparation, and keeps the visit fixed on Wednesday of week 3
10-design/week-1-plan.md is unchanged
No day plans or Thai core plans are written; the reply offers or names them as the next step for this unit rather than writing them
Every session in the week 2 plan carries light universal UDL options rather than ability tiers
No student names appear anywhere

evals.prompt: Please plan my meteorology main lesson block: the block plan and the week plans. The anchor and the units are in my draft.
evals.expected_output: Without a request for an anticipated route, the fixed sequence stays the default: the draft block plan updated in place with every unit marked fixed in the teacher's order, and all three week plans written now. The anticipated route may be mentioned as an option but is not used.
expectations: The block plan is written in 10-design/block-plan.md (updated in place) and week plans for weeks 1, 2 and 3 exist in 10-design/
The units run in the teacher's order (air on the move, ocean currents, putting it together: the monsoon) and each is marked or described as fixed
No unit is marked interchangeable, and the plan does not say the driving question board chooses the order of units
All three week plans are fully written now, none left waiting for a board choice
